title: 3D Agar.io one-shot: Anthropic vs OpenAI
author: sw3d
selftext:
I saw [this post](https://www.reddit.com/r/SoloDevelopment/comments/1ww4kdy/i_created_a_3d_version_of_slitherio/) and somebody thought it would be cool to see a similar take but in 3D. There's agar3d dot io which looks nice but is actually an isometric (not true 3D) and a few other attempts I've seen, but nothing quite hits on the gameplay/visuals/3Dness. So I thought I'd test out Claude and Codex, it seemed like a simple enough game but with some depth on both frontend and backend. Claude video here, codex in comments. Both produced functional games in about half an hour. Including multiplayer. Of course, this is visually a very simple game but still interesting. One is clearly better and if you've been doing AI game dev I bet you know which is which :)

Prompt:

"I want to make a 3D version of agar.io (multiplayer, you start with a blob that can move aorund, eat little pellets to grow and eat other players by taking up more than 50% of their "space", press space to split off into more blobs). It should be just like agario the 2D game except in 3D space. use procedural graphics for everything. should run smoothly in a web browser, Rust-based webserver that can be deployed to my homebox or cloudflare (homebox.sh). plan it out then use sol subagents to execute and have them check their work, then you verif collectively and iterate. you can read ../blitz (functional multiplayer game that can be a reference for websocket/homebox/server stuff, but dont reuse any of blitz engine, make your own)"
